technical_facts: Cells became rockets on level cross
Implemented lookspring, lookstrafe, and mouse y invert checkboxes
FOV is no longer a saved cvar
Implemented wizspike and knightspike t ents
Implemented end of episode text and removal of items after episode completion
Fixed head gib eye in floor bug
Managed surface cache size in weird aspect ratio modes
Prevented video buffer allocation from causing subsequent load failures
Implemented push for red super spikes
personality_patterns: Attention to detail regarding UI/UX (e.g., right-justifying text, cursor blinking)
Focus on technical stability and stability across different hardware configurations (aspect ratios, buffer allocations)
Systematic approach to bug fixing and bug tracking (the .plan file format)
Prioritizing functional correctness over aesthetic preference (e.g., changing name back to quad damage)

gnosis_principles.description: The process of continuous, small-scale adjustments to trigger systems, sound attenuation, and physics (gibbing, knock down code) to achieve a polished final product.

heritage_patterns: Use of .plan files for public-facing development logs
Low-level memory and buffer management for graphics drivers/video buffers

dpo_pairs.prompt: What did John Carmack change regarding the FOV in the 1996-06-08 plan file?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He made FOV not a saved cvar.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He updated the FOV settings to be saved in a saved cvar.
